sections.label: Who we are
sections.heading: Look for the system behind the symptom.
sections.body:
Fox Consulting Group is led by Justin Fuchs, who has spent nearly 20 years on the infrastructure side of marketing: strategy, analytics, platforms and the operating models that hold them together. Since 2016 the practice has delivered 30+ engagements for organizations including Altair, Corewell Health, Gordon Food Service and Allstate Identity Protection, and most clients have stayed five years or more.

Most recently, Justin built a hub-and-spoke analytics function across 13 business units at a public manufacturer, taking reporting from months to days. He’s as comfortable presenting a roadmap to a segment president as he is debugging the tag manager himself. You work with him directly, with a small bench of trusted specialists when the work calls for it.

servicePages.title: Digital Strategy Consulting
servicePages.heroSummary: Build a unified digital program that connects business priorities to channels, technology, measurement, and the work your team does every day.

problem.heading: Tactics move faster when the strategy underneath them is clear.
problem.body: Most teams do not need more ideas. They need a shared view of where digital marketing creates value, which opportunities deserve attention, and how people, process, and technology should work together. We turn that ambiguity into a practical operating roadmap.

capabilities.title: Channel planning
capabilities.body: Evaluate the channels that matter, clarify what each should accomplish, and build playbooks teams can actually use.

capabilities.title: Marketing technology strategy

capabilities.title: Leadership advisory

servicePages.title: Marketing Operations & Governance
servicePages.heroSummary: Design the team structure, workflows and governance that let marketing scale across brands and business units, without everything routing through one overworked person.

problem.heading: Most marketing teams aren’t short on talent. They’re short on a system.
problem.body: As marketing grows across brands, regions and business units, the work fragments. Every team builds its own tools, definitions and approvals, and leaders spend their time reconciling instead of deciding. We design the operating model that pulls it back together, without forcing every team into the same mold.

capabilities.title: Operating model design
capabilities.body: Centralized, federated or hub-and-spoke: define what the center owns, what each team owns, and how decisions move between them.

capabilities.title: Workflow and intake
capabilities.body: Map how work actually flows today, remove the friction, and stand up intake and prioritization that teams will really use.

capabilities.title: Web, social and platform governance
capabilities.body: Standards for who can publish, launch, buy and access what, across every site, account and platform the organization runs.

capabilities.title: Change management and enablement
capabilities.body: Training, playbooks and rollout plans that help new ways of working stick once the engagement ends.

approach.heading: Start with how the work really happens.
approach.body: We build on the team you have, not an org chart from a slide deck.

steps.title: Observe
steps.body: Interview teams and stakeholders, and trace how requests, approvals and launches move today.

steps.title: Design
steps.body: Define roles, decision rights, standards and the workflows that connect them.

steps.title: Pilot
steps.body: Prove the model with one team or brand before asking everyone to change.

steps.title: Scale
steps.body: Roll out with training, documentation and a governance rhythm that keeps it current.

outcomes: Clear ownership and decision rights across teams
Fewer one-off tools and duplicate processes
Governance that reduces platform and access risk
A model that scales as brands and teams are added

cta.heading: Build the system behind the team.
cta.body: Tell us how your marketing organization is structured today and where it’s starting to strain.

meta.title: Marketing Operations & Governance Consulting
meta.description: Marketing operations consulting: team structure, workflows and governance that let marketing scale across brands and business units without everything routing through one person.

servicePages.title: Marketing Technology Strategy
servicePages.heroSummary: Choose, implement and govern the platforms your marketing runs on, so the stack serves the strategy instead of the other way around.

problem.heading: More platforms rarely means more capability.
problem.body: Stacks grow one urgent purchase at a time. Before long the CRM, CMS, analytics, consent and ad tools overlap, integrations are fragile, and nobody can say what each license is for. We help teams decide what they need, select it on evidence, and implement it with the people who’ll use it.

capabilities.title: Stack assessment
capabilities.body: Inventory what you own, what it costs, how it connects and how much of it is actually used.

capabilities.title: Platform selection
capabilities.body: Requirements, evaluation criteria and vendor scoring for CRM, CMS, marketing automation, consent and analytics platforms.

capabilities.title: Implementation leadership
capabilities.body: Translate business needs into technical requirements, and keep vendors, IT and marketing aligned through launch.

capabilities.title: Vendor and license management
capabilities.body: Consolidate overlapping tools and find the contract structure that fits how your organization buys.

approach.heading: Decisions first, demos second.
approach.body: The right platform depends on your operating model, your team’s skills and what you need to measure, not on the best demo.

steps.title: Inventory
steps.body: Document the current stack, its costs, integrations and owners.

steps.title: Define
steps.body: Agree on requirements and evaluation criteria with marketing, IT and the business.

steps.title: Select
steps.body: Run a structured evaluation and build the business case.

steps.title: Implement
steps.body: Lead requirements, integration planning and adoption through launch.

outcomes: A stack that maps to clear business needs
Platform decisions backed by documented criteria
Cleaner integrations and fewer overlapping licenses
Implementations that teams actually adopt

cta.heading: Make the stack earn its keep.
cta.body: Whether you’re replacing one platform or untangling the whole stack, we can help you find the next sensible step.

servicePages.title: Analytics & Measurement
servicePages.heroSummary: Build a measurement system your team trusts, understands and uses, with privacy and consent designed in from the start.

problem.heading: A technically valid setup is not the same as useful analytics.
problem.body: GA4 often arrives with duplicated events, unclear conversions and reports no one confidently uses, while consent rules and browser changes keep shrinking what you can track. We connect each measurement decision to a question the organization actually needs answered, and design it to stay useful with less invasive tracking.

capabilities.title: KPI frameworks
capabilities.body: Connect business goals to the metrics, events and conversions that show progress, with one agreed definition per KPI.

capabilities.title: GA4 and tag management
capabilities.body: Audit, plan and implement GA4 and Google Tag Manager, with naming, ownership and testing documented.

capabilities.title: Privacy-first measurement
capabilities.body: Consent-aware implementation and platform evaluation (Google Analytics, Piwik PRO, Matomo and others) matched to your risk profile.

capabilities.title: Reporting and dashboards
capabilities.body: Focused Looker Studio and Power BI reporting that makes performance understandable to the people using it.

capabilities.title: AI-assisted reporting
capabilities.body: Automate the recurring data wrangling so analysts spend their time on interpretation, not copy and paste.

approach.heading: Measure what matters, then make it usable.
approach.body: We begin with decisions and business questions—not a generic event checklist.

steps.title: Define
steps.body: Clarify the audiences, journeys, outcomes, and decisions the measurement system must support.

steps.title: Audit
steps.body: Inspect the current implementation and identify gaps, noise, risk, and unreliable reporting.

steps.title: Implement
steps.body: Configure, test, document, and govern a durable event and conversion framework.

steps.title: Operationalize
steps.body: Build reporting rhythms and train teams to turn analytics into action.

outcomes: A documented, governed measurement plan
Cleaner event and conversion data
Reporting that holds up with less invasive tracking
Greater confidence and adoption across the team

cta.heading: Make your analytics useful again.
cta.body: Whether you need an audit, a cleaner implementation or a privacy-first approach, we can clarify the next step.

servicePages.title: On-Demand Digital Consulting
servicePages.heroSummary: Get experienced, objective guidance for a specific digital marketing decision—without committing to a full consulting engagement.

problem.heading: Sometimes you need one clear conversation, not a twelve-week project.
problem.body: Leaders regularly face decisions that are too important to make alone but too focused for a traditional engagement. On-demand sessions create space to pressure-test a plan, diagnose a problem, or find the next best move.

capabilities.title: Strategy review
capabilities.body: Bring a plan, roadmap, or recommendation and get direct, experienced feedback before you commit.

capabilities.title: Analytics troubleshooting
capabilities.body: Work through measurement questions, reporting gaps, platform choices, or implementation concerns.

capabilities.title: Technology decisions
capabilities.body: Clarify requirements, evaluation criteria, and tradeoffs before selecting or replacing marketing technology.

capabilities.title: Leadership coaching
capabilities.body: Use the session as a confidential thought partnership for organizational, team, or prioritization challenges.

approach.heading: Focused preparation. Candid advice. A usable next step.
approach.body: Each session is structured around one decision or challenge so the time produces a concrete outcome.

steps.title: Submit context
steps.body: Share the question, relevant background, and any materials that will make the conversation productive.

steps.title: Meet
steps.body: Use the session to examine assumptions, alternatives, risks, and practical next steps.

steps.title: Move
steps.body: Leave with a concise summary of recommendations and a clearer path forward.

outcomes: Independent perspective from a senior consultant
A clearer decision and immediate next step
No long-term engagement required
Advice grounded in your actual context
